proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a sharp replication hierarchy for average effects, the full treated mixing law, and finite treated mediator-variance support. The math panel passed; D0.5 graded the completed identification-only package subfield with a 7.2 score ceiling against the 7.4 field threshold and found no bounded repair within scope. Observable recovery maps remain implicit in two theorem statements, and an estimator, conditioning analysis, rates, or application would require a new research program.
tldr: Two untreated baselines sharply identify treated average indirect and direct effects on the compact uniformly nondegenerate stable Gaussian mediation class, while one baseline fails even under randomized adoption and known homoskedastic innovations. For full treated mechanism distributions, a strictly larger stable Gaussian class requires only \(C\succeq0\) and positive mediator variance \(a=C_{11}>0\) almost surely; it permits singular innovation covariance, noncompact latent means and covariances, and no moment or uniform eigenvalue lower-bound condition. Its sharp frontier is two-versus-three: compact countermodels show failure with two baselines, and three identify the treated mixing law by locally closed admissible-domain Laplace and Fourier uniqueness. On the original compact uniformly nondegenerate class, finite treated mediator-variance support sharpens the full-law frontier to one-versus-two. These are identification results, not estimation-rate claims.
gap: No inspected primary result gives this causal-target and volatility-support replication hierarchy in a stable Gaussian mediation panel with arbitrary latent dependence.
